evaluations.rationale: Specifies the stakeholder need (create a game, name/description as content) without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: in a single multi-line text field

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific algorithmic decision (use the average) instead of the higher-level need to accept a consensus estimate.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete mechanism (import from spreadsheet) rather than expressing the general need to bulk-add stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism for password reminders (email) rather than the higher-level need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Refers to joining via a URL/page and entering name — prescribes the URL-based access mechanism and a specific join flow rather than the general need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Refers to 'cards' and selection mechanics (concrete UI metaphor/interaction) — a solution choice rather than the underlying need to change an estimate until reveal.
Requests ability to see each estimator's prior estimates (stakeholder need) without specifying implementation.
Asks to see who gave what estimates during the current round; does not mandate technical choices.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete solution (a two-minute visible countdown timer) including duration and visible mechanism rather than just the need to limit discussion time.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific timer behavior (two-minute, auto-reset on play) — an implementation detail.
Requests the ability to scroll through prior rounds (user need) without prescribing specific UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Mandates a specific UI artifact/ordering (cards order) which is a design/implementation decision rather than a pure stakeholder need.
States the need to change estimate before draw completion; does not prescribe UI widgets or implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete UI presentation (thumbnail near cards) — a design/implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific technical standards/implementation technologies rather than expressing a stakeholder need at a problem level.
Requests a list of definitions (stakeholder need for shared understanding) without prescribing technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete implementation activity (database indexes) rather than stating a performance-related stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Mandates specific browser versions (technical compatibility targets) — an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Specifies compliance with a particular standard (W3C guidelines) — a concrete solution/implementation choice.
Asks for quick responsiveness (user-perceived performance) without prescribing technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical/data encoding requirement (Unicode) rather than stating the general need to support multiple languages.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific implementation artifact (URL design) rather than expressing a general need for navigable/clear structure.

evaluations.evidence: stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete data storage/privacy implementation requirement (non-identifiable storage) rather than a higher-level research need; this imposes a solution constraint.
